subjects.title: CCAF 2 - Claude Code
subjects.description: Domain 2 (20%) - CLAUDE.md hierarchy, slash commands, hooks, permissions, headless mode, and CI/CD integration.

cards.question: List the CLAUDE.md scopes and explain how they combine.
cards.answer:
Four scopes, loaded from **broadest to most specific**:

| Scope | Location |
|---|---|
| **Managed policy** | `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` (Linux/WSL), `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` (macOS), `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` (Windows) |
| **User** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` - you, across every project |
| **Project** | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` - committed, team-shared |
| **Local** | `./CLAUDE.local.md` - your personal, gitignored project notes |

The critical detail: they are **concatenated into context, not overridden**. Everything discovered is present; the more specific file simply appears **later**, and later instructions carry more weight when they conflict. Claude Code also walks **up** the directory tree from the working directory, loading every `CLAUDE.md` it passes, and loads files in **subdirectories on demand** when it reads files there.

Managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by user settings.
hints: Four locations. The verb that matters is concatenate, not override.

cards.question: A CLAUDE.md rule is being applied inconsistently. How do you diagnose and fix it?
cards.answer:
Work down four layers, in order:

1. **Is it even loaded?** Run **`/memory`** to see which memory files actually loaded this session. The most common cause is a rule sitting in **user-level** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` - which is not shared through version control, so a new teammate never receives it - when it belongs at **project level**.

2. **Is it drowning?** A large monolithic CLAUDE.md dilutes every instruction in it. Split it into topic-specific files under **`.claude/rules/`** (`testing.md`, `api-conventions.md`, `deployment.md`), or use **`@import`** to pull in only the standards each package needs.

3. **Is it relevant everywhere?** If it only applies to some files, path-scope it: a `.claude/rules/` file with YAML frontmatter `paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"]` loads **only** when matching files are edited. Always-loaded universal standards stay in CLAUDE.md; everything else is on-demand.

4. **Does it need a guarantee?** Then it was never a memory file. Instructions have a non-zero failure rate; **programmatic enforcement** - a prerequisite gate, or a hook that intercepts the tool call - is what makes compliance deterministic.
hints: Start by proving it loaded at all. There is a command for exactly that.

cards.question: How do you create a custom slash command, and what does its frontmatter control?
cards.answer:
A markdown file whose **filename becomes the command name**, in one of two scopes:

- **`.claude/commands/review.md`** -> `/review`, **project-scoped**: shared with the team through version control.
- **`~/.claude/commands/review.md`** -> `/review`, **user-scoped**: personal, available in every project.

Subdirectories namespace it: `.claude/commands/git/sync.md` -> `/git:sync`.

The body is the prompt; `$ARGUMENTS` receives everything typed after the command name and `$1`, `$2` the positional arguments. Frontmatter tunes the rest:

```markdown
---
description: Review a PR against our checklist
argument-hint: <pr-number>
allowed-tools: Bash(gh pr view:*), Read, Grep
---
Review PR #$1. Check error handling, tests, and naming.
```

- **`argument-hint`** prompts the developer for the parameter when they invoke it bare.
- **`allowed-tools`** restricts tool access during execution - least privilege for this command only.

The same frontmatter options apply to **skills** in `.claude/skills/`, which also support `context: fork`.
hints: The filename names it. The frontmatter decides what it may touch.

cards.question: What do Agent SDK hooks do, and when do you choose one over a prompt instruction?
cards.answer:
Hooks intercept the tool-call cycle and run **your** code, outside the model's judgement. Two patterns the exam names:

- **`PostToolUse`** - intercept tool **results** and transform them **before the model processes them**. The canonical use is normalizing heterogeneous formats: one MCP tool returns Unix timestamps, another ISO 8601, a third numeric status codes. Normalize at the hook and the agent never has to reason about the difference.
- **Outgoing tool-call interception** - block a policy-violating action and redirect. Refund above $500? The hook blocks the call and routes it to the human escalation workflow.

When to choose a hook: **when the rule must hold every time**. A prompt instruction gives you probabilistic compliance - usually followed, with a non-zero failure rate. A hook gives you a deterministic guarantee, because the model is not in the enforcement path at all.

So: business rules, compliance limits, and data normalization are hooks. Style, tone, and preference are prompts.
hints: One pattern rewrites what comes back; the other blocks what goes out.

cards.question: How do you run Claude Code non-interactively for automation?
cards.answer:
**Headless mode**, with `-p` / `--print`: Claude runs the prompt, prints the result, and exits.

```bash
claude -p "Review the staged diff and list blocking issues" \
  --output-format json \
  --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Bash(git diff:*)" \
  --permission-mode acceptEdits
```

Key flags:
- `--output-format` - `text` (default), `json` (one result object with cost and session id), or `stream-json` (events as they happen).
- `--allowedTools` / `--disallowedTools` - the permission surface for this run.
- `--permission-mode` - e.g. `plan`, `acceptEdits`.
- `--append-system-prompt` - inject instructions at the system-prompt level.
- `--resume <session-id>` / `--continue` - keep going from a previous run.

Headless mode **does not persist between runs** unless you resume a session, and it is the building block for CI jobs, git hooks, and batch scripts. Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions` outside an isolated container.
hints: One flag makes it a one-shot command; another makes the output parseable by the next step.

cards.question: How are MCP servers scoped in Claude Code, and how do credentials stay out of git?
hints: One file is committed, one is yours. Both load at the same time.

cards.question: What lives in the `.claude/` directory, and what decides which file a given instruction goes in?
cards.answer:
```text
.claude/
├── CLAUDE.md      # always-loaded universal standards (or root CLAUDE.md)
├── rules/         # topic files; YAML `paths` globs load them conditionally
├── commands/      # slash commands, project-scoped via version control
├── skills/        # SKILL.md + assets, loaded on demand
└── agents/        # subagent definitions: description, prompt, tool limits
```

Plus **`.mcp.json`** at the repo root for shared servers, and **`~/.claude.json`** outside the repo for your personal ones.

The routing question is **how often the instruction is relevant**:

| Relevance | Home |
|---|---|
| Every session, universal | `CLAUDE.md` |
| Only when editing matching files | `rules/` with a `paths` glob |
| Only when a specific task comes up | `skills/` |
| Only when a developer asks for it by name | `commands/` |

Path-scoped rules beat a subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` when the convention follows a **file type** rather than a directory - test files spread across the whole tree are the standard example.
hints: Sort the whole directory by one question: how often does this matter?

cards.question: What is the `@path` import syntax in CLAUDE.md and what is its limit?
cards.answer:
A CLAUDE.md can pull in other files with `@path/to/file`:

```markdown
See @README.md for the overview and @docs/git-workflow.md for branching rules.
```

Relative paths resolve against the **file containing the import**, not the working directory. Absolute paths and `~/` work too. Imported files can import further files, up to a maximum depth of **four hops**.

Two details that get tested:
- Import parsing **skips code spans and fenced code blocks**, so writing `` `@README` `` in backticks mentions the path without importing it.
- Imports **do not save context** - imported files are expanded and loaded at launch just like inline text. They are for organization. To actually reduce context, use **path-scoped rules** in `.claude/rules/` (loaded only when Claude touches matching files) or **skills** (loaded on demand).
hints: There is a hop limit - and a very common belief about context savings that is wrong.

cards.question: How do you define a custom subagent in Claude Code and why would you?
cards.answer:
A markdown file with YAML frontmatter in `.claude/agents/` (project) or `~/.claude/agents/` (personal):

```markdown
---
name: security-reviewer
description: Reviews a diff for security issues. Use after changes to auth or input handling.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: opus
---
You are a security reviewer. Focus on injection, authz, and secret handling.
Return findings as a list of file:line + severity + fix.
```

Why: **context isolation** (it works in its own window and returns a short result), **specialization** (a narrower system prompt beats a general one), **least privilege** (a reviewer gets no write tools), and **parallelism** (independent subagents run concurrently).

The `description` matters most - it is what the main agent reads to decide when to delegate. Write it as a trigger condition, not a title.
hints: A markdown file with frontmatter, where one field decides when it actually gets used.

cards.question: Your CLAUDE.md has grown to 600 lines and adherence is getting worse. What do you do?
cards.answer:
Long files consume context on every session and **reduce** adherence; the guidance is to target **under 200 lines**. Fixes, in order of value:

1. **Move path-scoped content to `.claude/rules/`** with `paths` frontmatter, so it loads only when Claude touches matching files:
   ```markdown
   ---
   paths: ["src/api/**/*.ts"]
   ---
   All endpoints validate input with Zod.
   ```
2. **Move multi-step procedures to skills**, which load on demand instead of every session.
3. **Delete what Claude can derive** from the codebase - directory listings, dependency lists, architecture recaps. Keep pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from the tool defaults.
4. **Remove contradictions**, including in ancestor and nested CLAUDE.md files.

What does **not** help: splitting into `@` imports. Imported files still load in full at launch, so the context cost is unchanged - only the file organization improves.
hints: Imports will not help. What actually loads on demand instead of at launch?

cards.question: Three MCP tools return dates as Unix timestamps, ISO 8601 strings, and numeric codes, and the agent keeps comparing them wrongly. What is the cleanest fix?
cards.answer: PostToolUse hooks intercept tool results for transformation before the model sees them, which is exactly the named use case for normalizing heterogeneous formats. Rewriting third-party servers is often not available to you; prompting makes the model do arithmetic it should never have been handed.

choices.text: A `PostToolUse` hook that normalizes each tool's result before the model processes it
A system prompt section explaining each tool's date format and how to convert between them
Few-shot examples showing correct date comparisons across all three of the tool formats
A rewrite of the three MCP servers so every one of them emits ISO 8601 timestamps

hints: Fix it once on the way in, or explain it forever in the prompt?

cards.question: You have a user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and a project `./CLAUDE.md`. How does Claude Code combine them?
cards.answer: Both are concatenated into context, ordered broad to specific, so the project file appears after the user file and carries more weight on conflicts. CLAUDE.md files do not override each other the way settings files do.

choices.text: Both load; the project file appears later in context and wins on conflicts
The project file replaces the user file entirely
The user file wins because user scope has higher precedence
Only the file nearest the working directory is loaded

hints: Do CLAUDE.md files replace one another, or pile up?

cards.question: A CI job must have Claude review every PR and emit machine-readable output for a downstream step. What is the right invocation?
cards.answer: Headless mode with `--print` and `--output-format json` gives a single structured result object the next step can parse. The `@claude` mention flow is interactive and only fires when a human writes a comment.

choices.text: `claude -p "..." --output-format json` with an explicit `--allowedTools` list
An interactive `claude` session in the runner
Post an `@claude` comment from the workflow and wait
`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` so nothing blocks the run

hints: "Every PR" eliminates one option; "machine-readable" eliminates another.

cards.question: Where do you put an MCP server config so the whole team gets it from version control?
cards.answer: `.mcp.json` at the repository root is the project scope - committed and shared. Claude Code asks for approval before using servers defined there, since it is configuration authored by other people.

choices.text: `.mcp.json` at the repository root
`~/.claude/settings.json`
`.claude/settings.local.json`
`CLAUDE.md`, as a documented setup step

hints: Version control means a committed file - and this one does not live inside .claude/.

cards.question: A file at `.claude/commands/deploy/staging.md` creates which slash command?
cards.answer: `/deploy:staging` - subdirectories namespace commands, and the filename is the command name.

choices.text: `/deploy:staging`
`/staging`
`/deploy/staging`
`/deploy staging`

hints: Subdirectories do something specific to the command name.

cards.question: Which skill frontmatter field prompts the developer for a parameter when the skill is invoked bare?
cards.answer: `argument-hint` supplies the expected-parameter hint shown when a developer invokes the skill without arguments. `allowed-tools` restricts tools, `context: fork` runs it in an isolated subagent, and `description` drives when Claude loads it.

choices.text: `argument-hint`
`allowed-tools`
`context: fork`
`description`

hints: The name says what it hints at.

cards.question: Your CLAUDE.md is too long. Which change actually reduces the context it consumes?
cards.answer: Path-scoped rules load only when Claude works with matching files, so they genuinely cut startup context. `@` imports are expanded and loaded at launch, so they reorganize without saving anything.

choices.text: Move sections into `.claude/rules/` files with `paths` frontmatter
Split it into several files pulled in with `@path` imports
Move the content into `CLAUDE.local.md`
Wrap the long sections in HTML comments

hints: Which option actually loads less at startup, rather than just reorganizing the files?

cards.question: What is the most important field in a custom subagent definition for getting it used at the right time?
cards.answer: `description`. The main agent reads it to decide whether to delegate, so it should read as a trigger condition ("use after changes to auth or input handling"), not as a title.

choices.text: `description` - it is what the main agent matches against to decide when to delegate
`model` - it determines quality
`name` - the main agent matches on the name
`tools` - without it the subagent cannot run

hints: The main agent has to decide to delegate. What does it read in order to decide?

cards.question: Which file name holds a project's committed, team-shared Claude Code instructions?
cards.answer: `CLAUDE.md`, at the repo root or in `.claude/`. `CLAUDE.local.md` is the gitignored personal variant.
hints: All caps, dot md - it sits at the repo root or inside .claude/.

cards.question: Which CLI flag runs Claude Code non-interactively for scripting (short form)?
cards.answer: `-p` (long form `--print`). Combine with `--output-format json` for machine-readable results.
hints: A single letter - short for print.

cards.question: Which file at the repository root defines MCP servers shared with the whole team?
cards.answer: `.mcp.json`. Claude Code prompts for approval before using servers declared there.
hints: A dotfile at the repo root, named after the protocol itself.

cards.question: Which directory inside `.claude/` holds custom slash commands?
cards.answer: `commands/` - each `.md` file becomes a command named after the file.
hints: Plural, and it is what you type after a leading slash.

cards.question: Which slash command shows which memory files actually loaded into the current session?
cards.answer: `/context`. Check the **Memory files** section - if your CLAUDE.md is not listed, Claude cannot see it.
hints: It shows you what is in the window right now.

cards.question: Match each CLAUDE.md scope to its location.
cards.answer: Load order runs broadest to most specific, and all of them are concatenated rather than overriding each other.
hints: Order them by breadth: the whole machine, then you everywhere, then the team, then just you here.

cards.question: Match each requirement to the Claude Code mechanism that satisfies it.
cards.answer: The recurring split: `CLAUDE.md` is always-loaded context, `rules/` is conditionally-loaded context, skills are on-demand workflows, and tool restrictions are the only thing that actually prevents an action.

matchPairs.left: Conventions for test files spread across the tree
A verbose analysis that must not pollute the session
Universal standards needed in every session
Diagnosing why an instruction never applied
Stopping a subagent from editing any file

hints: Sort into always loaded, conditionally loaded, on demand, and actually enforced.
